title: Research
text: My research is organized around a recurring analytical problem:

title: Research
text:
Scientific Processes
This research stream examines the temporal and structural dynamics of scientific recognition.
Current themes include:

scientific dormancy,
Sleeping Beauty phenomena,
awakening and knowledge transmission,
citation trajectories,
epistemic change,
structural validation of bibliometric signals.

title: Research
text:
Scholarly Infrastructures
This programme examines how infrastructures shape what becomes visible, citable, classifiable, and evaluable.
Current themes include:

bibliographic recognition,
research evaluation infrastructures,
document-type ingestion,
formal versus functional openness,
software citation,
preservation and documentary quality,
metadata and knowledge graphs.

title: Research
text:
Organization of Science
This stream focuses on the relationship between observable academic roles and underlying structures of labor, authority, mobility, and disciplinary fit.
Current themes include:

hidden labor in team science,
contributorship and credit,
academic inbreeding,
disciplinary fit,
researcher mobility.

title: Projects
text:
A multi-study research programme examining scientific dormancy, awakening, and post-awakening knowledge diffusion.
The programme asks:

What happens during dormancy?
What triggers awakening?
Does citation visibility correspond to structural transmission?
How does awakened knowledge reshape scientific fields?

Related studies include Epistemic Pollination, Dormancy as a Contact Process, and The Many Faces of Awakening.

title: Projects
text:
INFRAREC

Stabilizing Scholarly Objects in Knowledge Infrastructures
INFRAREC investigates the infrastructural conditions under which scholarly objects become recognizable, citable, indexed, and evaluable.
The project focuses on:

software citation objecthood,
bibliographic identity,
genre recognition,
graph connectivity,
infrastructural recognition.

title: Projects
text:
Research Evaluation Infrastructure
This programme examines how bibliographic infrastructures shape the populations and objects available for research evaluation.

title: Projects
text:
Labor and Credit in Science
This programme studies the relationship between scientific work, contributorship, authorship, authority, and academic organization.

title: Kemal Yayla
text:
I am an Assistant Professor at İzmir Kâtip Çelebi University, working at the intersection of bibliometrics, scholarly communication, research evaluation, and computational social science.
My research examines how scientific activity becomes visible, measurable, and evaluable through scholarly infrastructures.

title: Kemal Yayla
text:
Research programme

Scientific Processes
I study citation dynamics, delayed recognition, Sleeping Beauties, awakening processes, and epistemic change.


Scholarly Infrastructures
I examine open science, bibliographic recognition, research evaluation infrastructures, software citation, documentary quality, and machine-facing visibility.


Organization of Science
I study scientific labor, contributorship, academic mobility, disciplinary fit, and institutional structures.
